    <item>
      <title>Kongen fullførte maraton på tiden 4.43.01</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/kongen-fullforte-maraton-pa-tiden-4.43.01-1.18076803</link>
      <description>Kongen og kronprinsessen er deltakere i French Riviera Marathon, i Nice sør i Frankrike.
Kong Haakon løp i mål på tiden 4.43.01, ifølge sporingstjenesten Trackanza.
Det var TV 2 som meldte saken først.
Et bilde viser kongen og kronprinsessen løpende ved siden av hverandre under maratonet. I maratonet er kronprinsessen registrert som Ingrid Alexandra og kongen som Haakon Magnus.
Startskuddet gikk klokka 09.16, og distansen er helmaraton på 42,125 kilometer. Løypen går langs den franske rivieraen fra Nice til Cannes.
Lørdag formiddag opplyste Slottet på nettsidene sine at «statsrådet forestår bestyrelsen av riket».
Ifølge nettsidene var kongen og kronprinsessen på privat opphold i utlandet. Det betyr at regjeringen har ansvaret for å styre og forvalte landet.
(NTB/NRK)</description>

    <item>
      <title>Ny norsk gulltriumf i VM i skyting</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/ny-norsk-gulltriumf-i-vm-i-skyting-1.18076796</link>
      <description>Caroline Finnestad Lund, Jeanette Hegg Duestad og Synnøve Berg tok laggullet på 50 meter rifle match i VM i skyting i Doha søndag.
Det var Lunds andre gull i mesterskapet. Lørdag ble 21-åringen verdensmester på 50 meter 60 skudd liggende.
Norge sanket totalt 1764 poeng under lagkonkurransen, og de kom 3,0 poeng foran Sveits på 2.-plass. Tsjekkia stakk av med bronsemedaljen. De var to poeng bak sveitserne igjen.
I eliminasjonen for lag 1 ble Finnestad Lund nummer fire med 588 poeng. Synnøve Berg ble nummer sju med 586 poeng. Duestad ble nummer tre med 590 poeng i lag 2.
Alle de tre norske jentene er videre til kvalifiseringen i den individuelle konkurransen i den samme øvelsen mandag. (NTB)</description>

      <title>Flere skadet etter kraftig jordskjelv sentralt i Japan</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/flere-skadet-etter-kraftig-jordskjelv-sentralt-i-japan-1.18076688</link>
      <description>Minst 22 personer ble skadet da et jordskjelv med styrke 5,5 rammet Shizuoka-prefekturet i det sentrale Japan. Butikkvinduer ble knust, og folk rømte ut av bygninger.
Ifølge kringkasteren NHK er det ikke fare for tsunamier.
Skjelvet inntraff rundt klokka 1 natt til søndag. Det hadde en dybde på 41 kilometer. Den foreløpige målingen fra Japans meteorologiske institutt, som har ansvaret for overvåking og varsling av jordskjelv, var på 5,7.
Det amerikanske jordskjelvsenteret USGS målte det til 5,5.
I naboprefekturet Aichi ble det målt kraftige rystelser på nivå 5+ på den japanske skalaen – det sterkeste som er registrert der siden 1997.
(NTB)</description>

      <description>Israels president har gitt opposisjonsleder Gadi Eisenkot i oppdrag å prøve danne regjering.
Hverken partiene som støtter statsminister Benjamin Netanyahu eller partiene som støtter Eisenkot fikk flertall ved valget 27. november.
Netanyahus blokk fikk 53 plasser i Knesset, mens blokken til Eisenkot fikk 48 mandater.
For å få flertall og bli statsminister trenger man 61 plasser i nasjonalforsamlingen. Begge blokkene er avhengig av de 19 mandatene fra de palestinsk-arabiske partiene, mend både Netanyahu og Eisenkot har sagt de ikke vil forhandle med dem.</description>

      <description>Casper Ruud har storspilt i Paris denne uken. Nå er han klar for semifinale etter seier over Nuno Borges.
Ruuds oppgjør mot portugiseren endte med 7-6 (7-5), 6-4. De to møttes for bare ni dager siden i Basel, og da snudde Borges kampen til seier.
Ruud og Borges kom til semifinalen proppfulle av selvtillit: Ingen har tapt ett sett på veien, og de hadde heller ikke gitt fra seg mer enn fire game i noen av settene.

      <description>Politiet opplyser at det har vært en front-mot-front-ulykke på E6 like ved Eidsvoll-tunnelen i sørgående løp.
Ulykken skjedde ved kryss nummer 56 Boksrud. En av bilene kjørte nordover i det sørgående løpet, ifølge politiet.
Det satt en person i hver av bilene. En av dem er bekreftet død, den andre er kritisk skadet.
Det var tåke og svært glatt på stedet da ulykken skjedde.
E6 har midlertidig omkjøring i sørgående retning. Omgjøringen går fra kryss nummer 56 Boksrud via FV1551 Trondheimsveien, og deretter ut på E6 sydgående ved Nebbenes, opplyser politiet.</description>

      <description>Thomas Markle ble pågrepet av føderale agenter i nærheten av Tampa i Florida fredag morgen amerikansk tid.

Meghan Markle har nylig sagt at hun er «dypt fortvilet» over påstandene om at en samling overgrepsbilder av barn skal ha blitt funnet i farens tidligere hjem.

    <item>
      <title>NFF innfører semiautomatisert offside i Eliteserien</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/nff-innforer-semiautomatisert-offside-i-eliteserien-1.18075445</link>
      <description>Det opplyser Fotballforbundet på en pressekonferanse fredag.
– Prisen har kommet ned til et nivå som gjør at muligheten er der, sier generalsekretær Karl-Petter Løken.
Han opplyser at innføringen vil skje i tråd med et dommerløft. NFF bevilger 5,5 millioner kroner i 2027 til dommerløftet, og 3,5 millioner av dem skal få til semiautomatisert offside.
NFF ønsker å øke dette til 7,5 millioner kroner i 2028, og gradvis trappe opp mot 2030.
– Det du har sett med disse linjene blir borte og du får disse visningene med menneskekropper hvor du ser helt tydelig at det er offside. Det er semiautomatisert offside. Det er det ene løftet, sier Løken og fortsetter:
– Det er en utgift som tas én gang og som vil følge oss, og så vil vi trappe opp resten av investeringen i dommerutviklingene i de andre tiltakene i tillegg. Så det blir en gradvis opptrapping, eksempelvis profesjonalisering. Vi starter stille og rolig og så blir det flere og flere.
Dette skjer etter et VAR-oppgjør blant flere toppklubber. Roenborg satt ned et eget utvalg som konkluderte med at «Dagens VAR fungerer for dårlig under norske forhold. De lovte forbedringene har ikke løst hovedutfordringene, og kostnadene er for høye i forhold til kvaliteten».
Utvalget til Rosenborg stilte seg også tvilende til at semiautomatisert offside ville hjelpe VAR i norsk fotball.
– Så det vil være penger ut av vinduet hvis tinget sier nei (til VAR)? spør NRK.
– Vi kommer ikke til å diskutere detaljer i den avtalen, svarer Klaveness.</description>
      <category>Sportsnyheter</category>

      <title>VG: Oslo kutter antall elsparkesykler og hever aldersgrensen</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/vg_-oslo-kutter-antall-elsparkesykler-og-hever-aldersgrensen-1.18074020</link>
      <description>– For at folk som kunne ha de samme mulighetene til å reise som før og kunne komme seg rundt uten å bruke bilen, så øker vi antallet elsykler, sier byrådsleder Eirik Lae Solberg (H) til VG.
Det totale taket for elektriske utleiekjøretøy forblir på 16.000, men antallet elsparkesykler kuttes fra 16.000 til maksimalt 12.000. De resterende 4000 plassene settes av til elsykler når byrådet nå lyser ut ny anbudskonkurranse.
Byrådet setter også en fast nedre aldersgrense på 16 år for både elsykler og elsparkesykler.
– Vi hever aldersgrensen til 16 år sånn at vi styrker tryggheten både for dem som bruker elsykler- og elsparkesykler og for fotgjengere, sier Solberg.</description>

After two days of storms, the weather finally cleared Sunday, and more people joined the search for Dakota Smith, who went missing on the Johnstone Strait north of Sayward Friday.

“He lives just on the east side of the river here in a small cabin and frequently goes out on the ocean in a small canoe with a small electric motor,” said Campbell River SAR manager Jeff Ternan. “He was heading out for a short trip on the water and didn’t come back so his family were concerned and they called RCMP and started the search.”

Watch the story below:

Loading the player...

A large search with helicopters and boats was initiated Friday and Dakota’s canoe was found six nautical miles away on the other side of the strait.

“So it travelled quite a bit in the storm that existed that day,” Ternan added.

Search teams are basing their search on the assumption that he fell out of the canoe in Friday’s windy weather.

“Yeah that’s the assumption we’re making that he somehow got separated from his canoe and hopefully got to shore, so we’re searching shorelines and trying to locate him for sure,” Ternan said.

Shorelines to the east and west of where the Adam River flows into Johnstone Strait have now been searched.

A drone team from Arrowsmith Search and Rescue joined the search Sunday.

His family says James “Dakota” Smith lives with his partner and their two young children on his ancestral territory, where he has been leading the reoccupation of Hiladi Village, a traditional Ma’amtagila village site on the east side of the Adam River where it flows into the Johnstone Strait.

He was last seen around noon on Friday when he went out in the canoe to dispose of elk bones in the ocean.

Friends of the family like Shawn Decaire have been searching near the mouth of the Adam River.

Decaire went to the area Friday night and searched in the dark.

“It’s hard to hang on to hope, you know. We’re well into 48 hours into this, but the family have continued to say how resourceful and strong Dakota was, and they’re all hanging on to hope for positive outcomes, but at this point any outcome would be positive for the family,” Decaire told CHEK News.

Frank Provencal is Dakota’s neighbour and has been scouring the shoreline in his small tin boat.

“Trying to help out, really it’s sad,” he said.” It’s pretty good seeing all the people come together actually helping to find him.”

Search teams continued to search the shoreline and water by boat and air Sunday and said they’ll continue to do so until they find him or are stood down by RCMP.

]]> 1360048 From menace to resource: The Ahousaht First Nation’s battle with the invasive green crab https://cheknews.ca/from-menace-to-resource-the-ahousaht-first-nations-battle-with-the-invasive-green-crab-1358967/ Mon, 09 Nov 2026 00:20:59 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1358967

From a distance, European green crabs look harmless, almost like a key ingredient in a rich crab cake or a steaming hot bowl of seafood chowder.

The post From menace to resource: The Ahousaht First Nation’s battle with the invasive green crab appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

From a distance, European green crabs look harmless, almost like a key ingredient in a rich crab cake or a steaming hot bowl of seafood chowder.

In reality, they are relentless ecological invaders, and on Canada’s West Coast, they are not welcome by some.

Watch the story below:

Loading the player...

“It’s an invasive species that has been brought over from Europe and it arrived in the early 1800s on the East Coast,” explains Head Tyee Hereditary Chief Hašeʔukmis (HA-SHI-AHK-MIS) of the Ahousaht First Nation.

According to the Nation, green crabs arrived in their territory around 1998. Since then, they have remained on high alert as a severe threat to aquatic habitats and the marine species the community relies on for food security.

A threat to habitat and native species

The destruction goes deep beneath the water’s surface.

“They really destroy eelgrass habitat, which gives an area for all life to flourish,” says Ryan Teremy, Guardian Program Director with Maaqutusiis Hahoulthee Stewardship Society (MHSS.) Teremy highlights how the green invaders disrupt local ecosystems. “They push out native species of crabs into deeper water as well, so they take away some of their really good rearing areas.”

The problem is national in scale. On the East Coast, where green crabs were spotted off Newfoundland nearly 20 years ago, local fishermen are locked in a daily battle to protect valuable lobster catches and local fisheries.

“They are killing everything else that’s in the water that everybody’s making a living at,” says East Coast fish harvester Ken Viscount.

The short-term funding cycle

In 2021, the Department of Fisheries and Oceans (DFO) provided nearly $2 million for four coastal Nations, including Ahousaht, to remove as many green crabs as possible.

Operating through the Maaqutusiis Hahoulthee Stewardship Society (MHSS), the Ahousaht Nation set up traps and successfully removed 596,000 green crabs over a four-year period. But now that the study period is over, the funding has stopped, and the Nation says it is left dealing with the exact same crisis.

“The DFO with these four-year studies… after they are done, they move on to another project,” Hašeʔukmis tells CHEK News with anger and frustration.

Story continues below…

Turning waste into growth

Faced with hundreds of thousands of captured crabs, the Nation is pushing back against federal guidelines that require them to dump the catch in landfills.

While a quick online web search reveals green crabs are edible and widely used in recipes elsewhere, federal rules prevent anyone from commercially harvesting them. Hašeʔukmis finds that restriction absurd.

“What can we use the green crab for?!” he asks. “Because the DFO wanting me to go to the landfill and the dump, I really thought that was ridiculous.”

Instead of letting the harvest go to waste, the Ahousaht Nation is pioneering a workaround: turning the invasive crabs into nutrient-rich fertilizer.

“We’re now giving the proper nutrients so that when we do go and replant trees, it will really take going forward,” Hašeʔukmis explains.

Looking toward self-reliance

The overarching frustration for the Ahousaht Nation is the lack of long-term vision from regulators in Ottawa. Teremy argues that if they were permitted to build a sustainable industry around green crab collection, whether for food or fertilizer, they could fund their own conservation efforts and would not need to rely on temporary government grants to fight the invasion.

Until the rules change, the traps will stay in the water, and the Nation will keep turning a coastal threat into new life for the territory.

Another round of powerful fall storms is expected to hit Vancouver Island and much of B.C.’s coast this week, bringing heavy rain, strong winds and an increased risk of localized flooding.

Environment Canada issued a special weather statement Sunday afternoon, warning that a series of potent storms will move through the region from Tuesday through Thursday.

The storms are expected to bring prolonged periods of heavy rainfall to Vancouver Island, the South Coast, Central Coast and North Coast, with higher elevations and mountainous areas forecast to receive the greatest amounts.

The incoming storms follow several low-pressure systems that have already battered coastal communities in recent days, bringing significant rainfall and widespread power outages.

Environment Canada says the additional precipitation could lead to water pooling in areas with poor drainage and worsen existing flooding concerns, particularly in communities already saturated by recent storms.

Gusty southerly winds are also expected in some areas.

Forecasters say there is still uncertainty surrounding exact rainfall amounts and which areas will be hardest hit. Rainfall warnings may be issued as the storms approach.

Residents are encouraged to clear leaves and debris from storm drains to help reduce the risk of localized flooding.

B.C.’s three major transportation agencies are offering free travel to veterans and military personnel on Remembrance Day to honour those who have served.

BC Ferries, BC Transit and TransLink will provide complimentary travel on Nov. 11, with some services extending the offer to other emergency personnel.

BC Ferries will offer free passenger fares to customers travelling in uniform or presenting official Canadian military identification. The offer does not apply to the Inside Passage, Haida Gwaii or Central Coast Connector routes.

B.C. seniors will also be able to travel free on Remembrance Day by presenting valid identification, including a BC Services Card, driver’s licence, BC Identification Card or birth certificate.

At 11 a.m., BC Ferries will observe two minutes of silence aboard vessels and at terminals to honour those who have served. Canadian flags will fly at half-mast, while digital screens will display “Lest We Forget.”

BC Transit will offer free rides on all scheduled routes and handyDART services in the Victoria region to active and retired military personnel, cadets and those with Army, Navy or Air Force Association cards.

Buses will operate on a regular Sunday schedule and display “Lest We Forget” on destination signs.

TransLink will also provide free transit across Metro Vancouver to veterans, active military members, police, firefighters, Canadian Coast Guard members, Department of Fisheries and Oceans officers and BC Ambulance Service personnel.

Eligible riders can present identification or travel in uniform and will not need to tap their Compass Cards.

BC Transit and TransLink are also encouraging passengers and staff to observe a moment of silence at or near 11 a.m.

]]> 1360030 B.C. soldier killed in base fire remembered as globe-trotter, car-lover and fearless https://cheknews.ca/b-c-soldier-killed-in-base-fire-remembered-as-globe-trotter-car-lover-and-fearless-1360026/ Sun, 08 Nov 2026 21:06:51 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1360026

]]>

A 23-year-old Canadian soldier was remembered Sunday as a globe-trotting, sporty and car-loving man with an infectious sense of humour and a fearless love for life.

A photo of Pte. Aidan Goulding sat in front of the hundreds of military personnel, family and friends who gathered at an armoury on a stormy day in Vancouver for his funeral.  

Goulding was one of the four soldiers killed last month after a grass fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta overtook troops during a training exercise. Thirty-nine others were injured, and many remain in hospitals in Edmonton and Calgary.

Goulding’s funeral started with soldiers carrying his flag-draped casket into the armoury, with the sound of a bagpipe cascading, and some words from a rabbi.

Sonia Monk, Goulding’s mother, then described his upbringing in North Vancouver with his brother, Wylder, who was also his best friend.

“They had each other’s backs,” she said. “Their relationship touched my heart deeply, and I was content in knowing that they would always be close.”

Growing up, he showed his competitive and curious side.

His family said in a statement he played many sports, including soccer and rugby, and developed a love for cars at a young age.

He spent many hours buying used cars, fixing them late into the night under the glow of a lamp on his family’s driveway and then reselling them.

The first car he fine-tuned was a used Chrysler 300C.

The modification: make it louder.

“He loved understanding how things worked and took great pride in making them his own,” his family said. 

He was also stylish.

Monk said her son asked to wear a white suit on his first day of Grade 4. When he turned 21, he asked for a gold suit.

“He was unapologetically himself, and I admired that,” his mom said.

After he joined the Canadian Armed Forces, Goulding felt like he found a place where he belonged.

“It gave him a sense of purpose, a family and a place he truly felt at home,” Monk said.

The family has also described Goulding as a globetrotter.

In his short life, he explored many parts of the world, including Mexico, Germany, Austria, Italy, Croatia, Malta, the Netherlands, England and Spain.

Reagan Goulding, the soldier’s aunt, said during the funeral that he often made those around him laugh.

She said it’s been hard knowing that he died at a young age.

“This is perhaps one of the hardest parts of losing someone so young,” she said. “It’s not just the memories we have lost, but the opportunity to make a relationship we still had time to build.”

She also remembered the other soldiers killed in the fire alongside Goulding.

They were: Pte. Hayden Lykkemark, 19, of Langley, B.C.; Sgt. Morgan Wong, 26, of Edmonton; and Pte. Shaun Farrell, 23, of Prince Albert, Sask.

“Aidan and his fellow soldiers will not be forgotten,” Reagan said.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 8, 2026

Sailor 1st Class Brayden Zunti, who serves aboard HMCS Vancouver, has been selected as the Royal Canadian Navy sentry for the 2026 Remembrance Day Sentry Program.

Zunti is one of 12 military and RCMP personnel chosen to perform ceremonial duties during the national ceremony.

Established in 1988, the program recognizes outstanding members of the Canadian Armed Forces’ Regular and Reserve Force, as well as the RCMP, for their dedication, professionalism and service to Canada.

This year’s ceremony will also mark the 150th anniversary of the Royal Military College of Canada, with Officer Cadet Quinn MacDonald selected to serve as Sentry Commander.

Other participants include representatives from the Canadian Army, Royal Canadian Air Force, Canadian Special Operations Forces Command, Canadian Rangers and Indigenous Council.

The annual ceremony takes place at the National War Memorial in Ottawa on Remembrance Day, honouring Canadians who served and sacrificed their lives in military service.
